question_text: Find the co-ordinates of the point on the parabola y² = 2x whose focal distance is 5/2.

mark_split.label: Find a and set up the focal distance

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and set up the focal distance
steps.margin_note: First mark, for a = 1/2 and x₁ = 2.
steps.why: The focal distance of any point on y² = 4ax is always x₁ + a, the same rule as 121.1 applied with a smaller a.
common_mistakes: Reading 4a = 2 as a = 2 instead of a = 1/2.
Losing the fraction when solving x₁ + 1/2 = 5/2 for x₁.
steps.memory_tip: Focal distance is always x-coordinate plus a — SP = x₁ + a, for any point on y² = 4ax.

steps.label: Solve for the point
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for both coordinates of the point.
steps.why: Once x₁ is known, y₁ follows straight from the parabola's own equation, giving two symmetric points about the axis.
common_mistakes: Giving only one value of y₁ and forgetting the ± sign.
Writing y₁ = 2x₁ instead of y₁² = 2x₁ before taking the square root.
steps.memory_tip: Every x on the curve gives two points, one above the axis and one below — always write the ± sign.

insider_note: The steps here are identical in shape to 121.1 with a smaller a — recognising the two questions as the same method is worth more than re-deriving the focal-distance rule from scratch each time.
